title: Error Envelope
description: The uniform failure response shape for every platform interface. It carries a stable machine-readable code, a message safe to show a client, optional structured detail, and the correlation identifiers needed to find the failure in observability data. It never carries stack traces, provider error payloads, credentials, or connection information.

success.title: Success discriminator
success.description: Always false. Present so a client can discriminate success from failure without inspecting a transport status code.

error.title: Error body
error.description: The machine-readable failure. 'code' is the compatibility-sensitive key; 'message' is for humans and may be reworded at any time.

code.title: Stable error code
code.description: The compatibility key. Consumers branch on this value, so changing or removing a published code is a breaking change. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, 3 to 64 characters, beginning with a letter. Codes are allocated by the service that owns the interface; this contract constrains their shape, not their meaning.

message.title: Client-safe message
message.description: A human-readable explanation safe to display. NOT a compatibility key: wording may change within a patch release and consumers must not parse or branch on it. Must not embed internal diagnostics, credentials, or personal data.
examples: The request could not be validated.

details.title: Structured detail
details.description: Optional structured, client-safe supplementary detail, such as which fields failed validation. Deliberately open so a service may add detail without a contract change; every value placed here must be safe to expose.

examples.reason: must be RFC 3339 with a UTC offset

error.message: The request could not be validated.

details.reason: must be RFC 3339 with a UTC offset
